# Introduction {#sec-introduction}

**Trust is the complement of verifiability — and above a floor, that
complement factors: verification fails for exactly three reasons, each
failure names whom you must trust and what the cure costs, and the count
is derived rather than stipulated, in a machine-checked biconditional
whose reverse direction *constructs* the evidence scheme.**

## The asymmetry that motivates the question

Every deployed verification system ships a trusted remainder: a
certificate authority, a genesis seed, a witness set, a key ceremony.
The field has deep machinery for what *can* be established. Gligor and
Woo prove that a software root of trust is reachable, unconditionally,
from an untrusted starting state [@gligor-woo-2019]. Protocol analysis
proves security goals — authentication, confidentiality — from minimal
executions, expressed as geometric sentences over a protocol's runs
[@dougherty-guttman-ramsdell-2018]. Formal e-voting verifiability
isolates exactly the fragment of a protocol that can be checked, leaving
the rest to an explicit trust assumption [@kremer-ryan-smyth-2010].

Three different subfields, and in each the remainder is handled the same
way: assumed, listed, never analyzed. Kremer, Ryan, and Smyth are
explicit about it — "we only model the parts of the protocol that we
need to trust for the purpose of verifiability; all the remaining parts
of the system will be controlled by the adversarial environment"
[@kremer-ryan-smyth-2010] — and the inference from *not verifiable* to
*therefore trusted* is their own, not one imposed on them from outside.
The pattern recurs at the level of individual papers: Dougherty,
Guttman, and Ramsdell build their entire technical contribution around
computing *minimal* executions, and never turn that minimality machinery
on the trust assumptions their own analysis holds fixed
[@dougherty-guttman-ramsdell-2018]. The field formalizes *establish* and
enumerates *assume* — consistently, across subfields that do not cite
one another.

The pattern is old enough to date. A self-maintaining compiler trapdoor
— one that survives recompilation because the compiler compiles itself —
was described and costed in the 1974 security evaluation of Multics
[@karger-schell-1974], ten years before the lecture that made it famous
[@thompson-1984]. The work since has shrunk that trusted base repeatedly
without bounding it, and bounding it is what @sec-instances does.

## The question folklore has always asked, never answered

Folklore has long said what the remainder *is*. For Frankel, trust
enters "where more exact knowledge is not available" [@frankel-1977];
for Lewis and Weigert it "begins where prediction ends"
[@lewis-weigert-1985]. These are the ancestors of this
paper's thesis-half, and the sociological and epistemological work
descending from them inherits the same unfactored formulation
(@sec-related-work).

Left unanswered: *why*? If the residue is structureless, "minimize
trust" is a slogan — a direction with no metric. If the residue has
causes, each cause carries its own impossibility grade, its own minimal
repair, and its own price, and "minimize trust" becomes an optimization
problem with a computable objective.

## The contribution, with its honest pedigree

Above a floor of two named residuals (@sec-floor), verification of a
claim over a growing, append-only record fails for exactly one of three
reasons:

- **Determination.** The fact is not a function of the committed record
  — the record underdetermines the history that produced it.
- **Certifiability.** The fact is in the record, but not certifiable
  from it at the verifier's computational power — semi-decidable
  ($\Sigma_1$) at the computable stratum, in $\mathrm{NP}$ at the
  polynomial one.
- **Monotonicity.** The fact does not stay true as the record grows —
  the evidence cannot endure past the moment it was produced.

Each axis is inherited, and credited as such. Archival diplomatics
hypothesized the opposite of the determination axis and reported it
refuted, across twenty-two case studies [@interpares-2002]; that finding
has already crossed into computer science once [@factor-et-al-2009].
Synthetic topology owns the algebra of the other two, taken together:
semi-decidable, upward-closed properties are the *observables* of that
tradition — certifiability and stability-under-extension bundled into
one notion, decades before this paper [@smyth-1983; @abramsky-1987;
@vickers-1989], in the effective, computably-enumerable-join form this
paper actually instantiates [@escardo-2004]. CALM owns the
coordination-freedom reading of monotonicity, itself a biconditional,
refereed for relational transducers and since generalized
[@ameloot-neven-vandenbussche-2013; @hellerstein-2026].

The composition is ours. No source we reached factors the residue *by
cause*, pairs these axes as a joint characterization of *trust*, or
states the biconditional form. And "exactly three" is derived: it is the
$\Leftarrow$ direction of a machine-checked if-and-only-if — satisfy all
three conditions, and the evidence scheme is *constructed* on the spot
out of them.

The failed axis identifies the trust anchor. A determination failure
names the witness of history — the signer, the attestor — who must be
trusted because the record alone cannot settle the question. A
certifiability failure names the judgment that substitutes for the
impossible check: a voucher. A monotonicity failure names the holder of
liveness on the present — a witness quorum, a gossip network. The
framework thereby *derives*, from the shape of the failure alone,
exactly the anchor inventory practice already converged on: certificate
authorities, vouches, transparency-log witnesses. @sec-instances works
one case in full — a split-view (equivocation) attack against an
append-only log — and shows the framework predicting the deployed
defense in detail, rather than naming a category after the fact.

Trust, on this account, is not eliminated but located, typed, priced,
and bounded: a system whose trusted remainder equals its named genesis
base sits *at* the verification ceiling, provably rather than by
inspection.

## Contributions

Every result below is machine-checked in Lean 4 and named at the point
it is stated; the development accompanies this paper as anonymized
supplementary material. There is no separate mechanization section
because there is nothing to segregate.

**C1.** The trichotomy as a biconditional, both legs proved, at the
oracle and computable strata (@sec-theorem: `trichotomy_ALL_iff`,
`trichotomy_snap_COMP_iff`, `comp_COMP_iff`). The polynomial stratum is
an open conjecture and is stated as one.

**C2.** The determination axis and its gate, non-vacuous
unconditionally (@sec-model, @sec-theorem: `determination_gate`,
`exists_undetermined_claim`).

**C3.** The factorization display, at the computable stratum and
enduring flavor: evidence-admitting claims are the effective observables
frame pulled back along the context-forgetting projection
(@sec-factorization: `factorization_COMP`). Separately, the
snapshot/enduring split *factors* the tradition's bundled "observable"
into two independent axes — this paper's own delta inside an inherited
algebra.

**C4.** The verification ceiling — a companion theorem, not a corollary
— over any well-founded justification structure admitting a record
realization, with the accounting and scheme worlds joined by a proved
relation rather than an analogy (@sec-instances: `Ceiling.ceiling`,
`RecordRealization`, `Discharges`). It is instantiated twice over one
neutral core: the identity instance discharges a content-carrying
realization from its own structure (`identityRealization`,
`principal_trust_bounded`), and the light source-integrity instance
instantiates over a content-neutral one (`suretyRealization`,
`surety_ceiling`).

**C5.** The cell table: eight nominal cells, two empty *by theorem*
rather than for want of a witness, six inhabited — one verifiable and
five flavors of trust, each with its own anchor, and each cure a move
along one of four coordinates (@sec-cell-table:
`undetermined_cell_empty`).

**C6.** Two usable forms of the theorem, each answering a question a
designer asks on its own (@sec-theorem). $\EALM$ — *Endurance As
Logical Monotonicity* — says what monotonicity buys: whether a
guarantee can rest on one self-contained certificate forever, or needs
refreshing (`endurance_iff_monotone`). The $\EON$ trilemma says what is
permanently lost when it cannot: of *Eternal*, *Offline*, and *Now*, a
verifier may have two (`eon_trilemma_impossibility`). Neither is deep,
and depth is not what a specialization is for.

The remaining sections carry the scaffolding these stand on:
@sec-model fixes the vocabulary, @sec-floor states the two residuals,
@sec-scope-objections states what is not claimed, and
@sec-related-work gives each ingredient its home.
